post.title: Say a Word Until It Breaks #shorts
post.description: Repeat a word over and over and it stops meaning anything. In 1907 psychologists Elizabeth Severance and Margaret Floy Washburn had people stare at a single word for three minutes; the words lost their meaning. Leon Jakobovits James named it semantic satiation in 1962. One explanation is that the brain's response to a word's meaning tires with repetition, then recovers when you stop. #psychology #shorts #brain #language
